title: Edgewise verdict sampler: low-cost per-hop capture and playback for routing decisions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Smart routing (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) currently lacks a practical, low-cost capture that lets engineers replay and debug decision paths without storing full request payloads. Existing per-hop traces are either too verbose (full request + embeddings) or too lossy (only final decision), making RCA and model-behavior analysis slow and expensive.

Goal: Implement an "edgewise verdict sampler" — a lightweight, policy-driven per-hop capture that records compact decision snapshots and deterministic playback hooks. Deliverables: 1) a compact per-hop schema, 2) a sampling policy engine (tier-aware + anomaly-adaptive), 3) storage/retention limits with cost estimates, 4) CLI/Console playback support and a dashboard for sample rates and coverage.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full request payload capture, PII enrichment, or long-term analytics pipelines (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: 1) New per-hop verdict logs are emitted for sampled requests with the compact schema and route-level references. 2) Sampling policy supports: customer-tier override, deterministic hash-based inclusion, anomaly-score-driven reservoir spikes, and a global rate cap. 3) Console playback can rehydrate a decision path (hop sequence) without request body and show why each hop chose its variant. 4) End-to-end latency impact <= 1.5% p50 and storage cost estimate validated with synthetic load. 5) Security review signed off for the minimal schema and retention policy.
design_notes:
Key trade-offs considered: full capture vs. compact verdicts. We prioritize compactness to keep storage and retrieval latency low: keep only metadata needed for deterministic replay and RCA (trace_id, hop_index, route_id, variant_id, model_version, rationale_tags, timing, region, tier, cost_units, fallback_reason).

Decision: Emit compact snapshots synchronously as structured logs (high-throughput append-only) and stream a sampled copy to the routing-observability store (S3/Parquet) for short-term playback (30d). For high-fidelity events during incidents, allow a manual burst sampling API.

Privacy: No request tokens, prompts, or embeddings in the default schema. Any request body capture must be opt-in and handled by a separate, audited path.
sampling_policy:
We will implement a hybrid sampling policy with these components: 
- Deterministic heatmap: 1-in-N sampling per customer request hash with N configurable by tier (P0: 1-in-50, P1: 1-in-200, Free: 1-in-1000). Deterministic hash ensures reproducible rollbacks.
- Anomaly reservoir: if a routing outcome crosses an anomaly threshold (e.g., unexpected fallback rate or SLO violation), route-level reservoir increases sampling up to X events/minute for 15 minutes.
- Manual burst API: SE/Oncall can trigger a 10m elevated-sampling window for a given customer/route.
- Global cap: hard global QPS cap (configurable) to protect storage pipeline.
The sampling controller runs in-route as a micro-decision; decisions are logged with sample_reason tags (deterministic|anomaly|manual|force).
data_schema:
Compact per-hop verdict schema (top-level fields):
- timestamp_iso (string)
- trace_id (string)
- parent_request_id (string)
- route_id (string)
- hop_index (string)
- tier (string)
- region (string)
- chosen_variant (string)  // e.g., model-7b-q4f-v2
- candidate_pool (comma-separated string) // short list of variant ids or tag hints
- model_version (string)
- latency_ms (string)
- cost_units (string)
- kv_cache_hit (string)  // true|false
- fallback_reason (string|null)
- decision_code (string)  // policy reason code (e.g., ROUTE_PREFER_LOCAL, FALLBACK_CAPACITY, QUOTA_EXCEEDED)
- rationale_tags (comma-separated string)
- sample_reason (string)  // deterministic|anomaly|manual|force
- retention_bucket (string)  // 7d|30d|90d
Note: All fields are strings to keep the log schema flat and compatible with existing ingestion.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): Implement schema and sampling engine behind a feature flag. Canary to 5 internal customers + 2 small external customers. Validate latency and storage metrics.
Phase 2 (gradual): Ramp deterministic sampling by tier over 2 weeks; enable anomaly reservoir. Turn on console playback in read-only mode.
Phase 3 (GA): Expose sampling controls to customer console, add manual burst API, increase retention buckets for enterprise customers as contract add-on.
Rollback: Feature flag off + drain store writers.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: sampling decisions (hash-based outcome determinism), sample_reason tags, and retention_bucket assignment.
Load test: simulate 50k RPS with realistic route mix to measure emitter latency and storage throughput.
Security: static schema scan to ensure no prompt/token fields are emitted. Create a red-team test that attempts to inject PII into logs and verify redaction policy.
Post-deploy: collect p50/p95/p99 of route path emission time and SLO alert for >1.5% latency regression.
metrics:
Emit these telemetry metrics to observability platform:
- routing.verdict.emit_count (by sample_reason, route_id, tier, region)
- routing.verdict.emit_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- routing.verdict.storage_bytes_ingested (per-hour)
- routing.verdict.reservoir_spike_events
- routing.verdict.playback_success_rate
- customer_coverage_by_tier (percentage of customers with at least one verdict in last 24h)
Use these metrics in console to drive alerts for storage budget overruns or sampling anomalies.
dashboards: Initial dashboards: 1) Verdict emission health: emit_count, latency, storage per route. 2) Sampling coverage heatmap (customers x routes). 3) Anomaly reservoir events timeline with corresponding SLO deviations. Example links (internal): Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROUTE/Edgewise+Verdict+Sampler, Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route-verdicts
